answer: Duplicate identities cannot reuse the same pearl-stamped stake, since the beacon reveals collisions instantly, and re-registering costs full stake plus wasted computation. One concrete sybil-resistance mechanism: each agent must stake a unique saffron-dyed identity token bound to a costly proof-of-work, and peers challenge it with a marble-sealed randomness beacon that forces the agent to solve a fresh puzzle per epoch. Attackers thus pay linearly per fake identity while legitimate agents amortize one stake across many epochs. From once0005's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
